title: Benefit Authorization, Caps and Allowances on Rental Property Service Contracts
content:
**B1.** On a Rental Property Service Contracts contract a benefit is authorized only after a covered determination is on file for the service request.

**B2. Repair or replace.** Bridgewell replaces when the repair estimate is at or above the tier's repair-to-replace threshold times the contracted replacement cost or the item cannot be repaired, and otherwise repairs.

**B3. Caps.** Caps apply per dwelling unit: each unit's item has its own cap, counted by the benefit already paid in the term on the same unit and item (authorizations less reversals, allowances excluded), and all payments on the contract share the aggregate term limit, counted by the benefit already paid on the contract in the term (authorizations less reversals). The term is the one in which the request date falls. The amount paid is the lowest of the work's cost, the remaining unit item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit, and never below zero; the work's cost is the repair estimate when the item is repaired and the replacement cost when it is replaced.

The item cap for each item is the tier's limit for that item:

| Item | Cap used |
|---|---|
| Heating system | the tier's heating system limit |
| Cooling system | the tier's cooling system limit |
| Ductwork | the tier's ductwork limit |
| Plumbing | the tier's interior plumbing limit |
| Water heater | the tier's water heater limit |
| Electrical | the tier's electrical system limit |
| Kitchen appliance | the tier's kitchen appliance limit |
| Laundry appliance | the tier's laundry appliance limit |
| Garage door opener | the tier's garage door opener limit |

**B4. Supplemental allowances.** Supplemental allowances pay the lower of the documented invoice amount and the allowance — the code-violation allowance, the permit fee allowance, the haul-away allowance on a replacement, the refrigerant allowance per term on a cooling repair, and the lead-safe work allowance when the year built is before 1978 and the work disturbs painted surfaces — count toward the aggregate limit only, and are paid at most once per type per request.

**B5. Cash in lieu.** When a like unit cannot be sourced, or the landlord asks for cash in place of an authorized replacement, cash in lieu equal to the contracted replacement cost within the same limits is offered; it is the landlord's decision, must be accepted no later than the tier's offer period in calendar days after the offer, is paid within the tier's payment period in calendar days, and replaces the replacement authorization, which is reversed in full. A tenant cannot accept cash in lieu or approve paying a difference above a cap.

**B6.** Only one repair, replacement or cash-in-lieu authorization is open per service request. An authorization is reversed in full when the work will not be performed and never after completion.

## Worked example (hypothetical request, threshold 0.60)

Water heater in Unit B, replacement cost $1000.00, repair estimate $650.00: $650.00 is at or above 0.60 times $1000.00 ($600.00), so Bridgewell replaces and the work's cost is $1000.00. The unit's water heater cap is $1000.00 with $300.00 already paid in the term, leaving $700.00; the aggregate limit has $500.00 left. The amount paid is the lowest of $1000.00, $700.00 and $500.00: **$500.00**.

## Lead-safe allowance, hypothetical buildings

A building from 1977 whose covered work disturbs painted surfaces meets the lead-safe condition: the year built is before 1978. The allowance then pays the lower of the documented invoice and the tier's lead-safe allowance, for example the lower of $180.00 and $150.00, which is $150.00, on Bridgewell Rental Combo Plus.
